subject.title: fix(agents): idle-timeout stalled provider response body reads

question: Should the exported provider JSON, text, and binary readers impose a 30-second idle timeout by default on all existing callers, or should timeout enforcement remain explicit per caller?
rationale: The bug fix is valid, but the default changes a shipped plugin SDK behavior and may reject previously accepted slow provider responses; tests alone cannot establish that this compatibility tradeoff is intended.

options.title: Approve shared default with proof
options.body: Adopt the 30-second shared default after adding controlled HTTP proof for stalled and slowly progressing bodies and recording owner acceptance of the SDK behavior change.

options.title: Require explicit caller opt-in
options.body: Keep the timeout option but preserve the existing default, then enable it only in internal caller paths with known response-latency contracts.

options.title: Accept the compatibility risk
options.body: Merge the global default as availability hardening while explicitly accepting that existing slow-response plugin callers may need to set a larger timeout.

recommendation.title: Approve shared default with proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the 30-second shared default after adding controlled HTTP proof for stalled and slowly progressing bodies and recording owner acceptance of the SDK behavior change.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged provider response-bounding and stalled-catalog work most directly established the contract being generalized.
